input.origin: Locally generated ezdxf R2010 scratch drawing described in p8d-librecad-native-ltype-isolated-2026-11-25.json.

positive.method: A scratch C++ dxfRW adapter read the three opted-in raw MATERIALs and their source dictionary, selected that dictionary and those three objects, generated one layer, supplied current-material and root dictionary entries, and remapped collisions. It produced an AC1024 ASCII DXF.
positive.observation: Independent ezdxf readback reports root C -> ACAD_MATERIAL F010, ByBlock F011, ByLayer F012, Global F013; all three owner and reactor links target F010; CMATERIAL F012 and RAWTEST, 0 and Defpoints layer material links target F013. Audit returned zero errors and zero repairs.

negative.method: The same writer omitted only Global while retaining the dictionary entry and layer pointers.
negative.observation: The writer returned success despite dangling F013 references. ezdxf left Global as an unresolved F013 string, found one INVALID_OWNER_HANDLE repair deleting the dictionary entry, and left the layer F013 pointer. Therefore this writer callback sequence is not a graph-closure guard.

limits: Both outputs and both probes are scratch-only; no third-party or generated DXF was committed.
This selected ASCII graph does not prove arbitrary DXF graphs, LibreCAD adapter behavior, binary output, mutation handling, native material meaning or full source-drawing preservation.

The negative control demonstrates the need for an explicit preflight and atomic refusal plus corrected retry before enabling consumer capture; it does not establish that generic dxfRW promises to validate arbitrary callbacks.
